grammarFocus: 第一、第二条件句的常见用途；建议与可能性的表达。
title: The Library Courtyard Renewal
instructions: 阅读以下关于社区图书馆庭院改造的模拟文章，回答10个问题。文章为模拟教育材料，非真实事件。题目类型包括单选、填空、匹配标题和判断正误/未提及。请根据文章内容作答，填空答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。
passage:
In the town of Riverton, the public library had a large but neglected courtyard. For years, it was used only for storing old furniture and broken equipment. The library manager, Mr. Patel, often looked at the courtyard from his office window and thought it could become a pleasant reading garden. However, the library had no extra money for such a project.

One afternoon, a regular visitor named Elena, who was a retired landscape architect, asked Mr. Patel why the courtyard was closed. When he explained the situation, Elena offered to help. She suggested forming a small group of volunteers to clean and redesign the space. Mr. Patel agreed, and they posted a sign-up sheet near the entrance. Within a week, fifteen people had signed up, including students, parents, and older residents.

The group held its first meeting in the library's meeting room. Elena presented a simple plan: the courtyard would have raised flower beds, a few benches, and a small area for children to read. She explained that if they used recycled materials, the cost would be much lower. The group decided to ask local shops for donations of wood and paint. They also agreed to organize a weekend clean-up day.

On the clean-up day, more than thirty volunteers arrived with gloves and tools. They removed the old furniture, pulled out weeds, and cleared the rubbish. By the afternoon, the courtyard was empty and clean. A local carpenter donated his time to build three wooden benches. A paint shop gave them several cans of outdoor paint in bright colours. The volunteers painted the walls and the benches, and the courtyard began to look welcoming.

Next, the group focused on the garden. Elena taught the volunteers how to plant flowers that need little water, such as lavender and rosemary. She explained that if they chose the right plants, the garden would survive even in dry summers. The group also installed a small noticeboard to display children's drawings and library news. Mr. Patel was delighted and said, "If we continue like this, the courtyard will be ready by the end of the month."

However, not everything went smoothly. One week before the opening, a water pipe broke and flooded part of the new garden. Some volunteers felt discouraged. Elena called an emergency meeting. She suggested that they ask the town council for help with the repair. The council sent a plumber the next day, and the pipe was fixed. The group also decided to add a simple drainage channel to prevent future flooding. This extra work took two more weekends, but the volunteers remained positive.

Finally, the courtyard opened to the public on a sunny Saturday in June. More than a hundred people attended the opening event. Children ran to the reading corner, and older residents sat on the benches and talked. The library now uses the courtyard for weekly story time and small community events. Mr. Patel said that the project had brought many new visitors to the library. Elena added, "If other towns want to do something similar, they should start with a small group and a clear plan."

The courtyard project shows how a community can solve problems by working together. It also shows that small actions, like donating paint or building a bench, can make a big difference. The library courtyard is now a favourite place for many people in Riverton.

questions.prompt: Why was the courtyard not used for reading before the project?
options: It was used for storing old furniture and broken equipment.
It was too small for reading.
answers: It was used for storing old furniture and broken equipment.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段提到，庭院多年来只用于存放旧家具和损坏的设备。
questions.evidence: it was used only for storing old furniture and broken equipment

questions.prompt: Who suggested forming a group of volunteers?
questions.explanation: 第二段提到，Elena建议成立一个志愿者小组来清理和重新设计空间。
questions.evidence: Elena offered to help. She suggested forming a small group of volunteers

questions.prompt: How many people signed up within a week? (one word)
questions.explanation: 第二段明确说明，一周内有15人报名。
questions.evidence: Within a week, fifteen people had signed up

questions.prompt: What did the group decide to ask local shops for?
questions.explanation: 第三段提到，小组决定向当地商店请求捐赠木材和油漆。
questions.evidence: The group decided to ask local shops for donations of wood and paint.

questions.prompt: What did a local carpenter donate?
options: His time to build three wooden benches
answers: His time to build three wooden benches
questions.explanation: 第四段提到，一位当地木匠捐出时间建造了三张木制长椅。
questions.evidence: A local carpenter donated his time to build three wooden benches.

questions.prompt: What kind of plants did Elena teach the volunteers to plant? (two words)
questions.explanation: 第五段提到，Elena教志愿者种植需要少量水的花，如薰衣草和迷迭香。填空答案来自原文“flowers that need little water”。
questions.evidence: Elena taught the volunteers how to plant flowers that need little water

questions.prompt: What problem happened one week before the opening?
options: A water pipe broke and flooded part of the garden.
answers: A water pipe broke and flooded part of the garden.
questions.explanation: 第六段提到，开放前一周，一根水管破裂，淹没了新花园的一部分。
questions.evidence: a water pipe broke and flooded part of the new garden

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A community solved problems together to create a library courtyard.
Elena is a retired landscape architect.
Local shops should donate more often.
answers: A community solved problems together to create a library courtyard.
questions.explanation: 文章整体讲述了社区如何通过合作解决问题，将图书馆庭院改造成一个受欢迎的空间。
questions.evidence: The courtyard project shows how a community can solve problems by working together.

questions.prompt: True or False: The town council paid for the new benches.
questions.explanation: 文章提到一位当地木匠捐出时间建造长椅，并未提及市议会支付长椅费用。因此该陈述与原文矛盾。
questions.evidence: A local carpenter donated his time to build three wooden benches.

questions.prompt: True or False: The library courtyard project inspired other towns to start similar projects.
questions.explanation: 文章提到Elena说如果其他城镇想做类似的事情，应该从小团体和明确的计划开始，但并未说明其他城镇已经受到启发并开始类似项目。因此该信息未提及。
questions.evidence: If other towns want to do something similar, they should start with a small group and a clear plan.

grammar.title: 第一、第二条件句的常见用途；建议与可能性的表达
grammar.explanation: 第一条件句（if + 一般现在时，主句用 will/can/may + 动词原形）用于表达可能发生的未来情况及其结果。第二条件句（if + 一般过去时，主句用 would/could/might + 动词原形）用于表达假设的、不太可能或与现在事实相反的情况。建议可以用 'should'、'could' 或 'why don't we...' 等表达。可能性可以用 'may'、'might'、'could' 等表达。
grammar.example: If we continue like this, the courtyard will be ready by the end of the month.

questions.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ______ the event indoors.
questions.explanation: 第一条件句表示将来可能发生的情况，主句用 will + 动词原形。

questions.prompt: If I ______ more time, I would join the gardening class.
questions.explanation: 第二条件句表示假设情况，if 从句用一般过去时。

questions.prompt: You ______ try the natural pest control method; it might work.
It ______ rain later, so bring an umbrella.
